examples.name: connection_basic
examples.title: Basic vSphere Connection
examples.description: Shows how to connect to vCenter using ClientBuilder with environment variables for credentials. This is the foundation for all vim_rs programs.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
anyhow = "1.0"

# Environment variables needed:
# VIM_SERVER=vcenter.example.com
# VIM_USERNAME=administrator@vsphere.local  
# VIM_PASSWORD=yourpassword

examples.name: property_collector_macro
examples.title: Property Collector with vim_retrievable Macro
examples.description: The RECOMMENDED way to fetch properties from vSphere objects. Uses vim_retrievable! macro to define a type-safe struct that maps to vSphere properties. Handles batching and type conversion automatically.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
vim_macros = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
anyhow = "1.0"
log = "0.4"
env_logger = "0.11"

# The vim_retrievable! macro generates:
# - Struct with specified fields
# - Automatic property collection
# - Type-safe property access
# - Batched retrieval for performance

examples.name: property_collector_raw
examples.title: Property Collector Raw API
examples.description: Low-level PropertyCollector API usage with manual PropertyFilterSpec. Use this for advanced scenarios or when you need fine-grained control. For most cases, prefer the vim_retrievable! macro.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
anyhow = "1.0"

# Use this for:
# - Complex traversal specs
# - Dynamic property selection
# - Advanced filtering
# Otherwise use vim_retrievable! macro

examples.name: vim_updatable_cache
examples.title: Real-time Property Monitoring with vim_updatable
examples.description: Monitor vSphere objects for property changes in real-time using vim_updatable! macro and CacheManager. Receives callbacks when objects are created, updated, or deleted.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
vim_macros = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
log = "0.4"

# vim_updatable! is for:
# - Real-time monitoring
# - Change detection
# - Event-driven updates
# Use vim_retrievable! for one-time fetches

examples.name: events_monitoring
examples.title: vSphere Event Monitoring
examples.description: Retrieve and monitor vSphere events using EventManager and EventHistoryCollector. Useful for auditing, alerting, and tracking infrastructure changes.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
anyhow = "1.0"
log = "0.4"
chrono = "0.4"

# Events useful for:
# - Audit trails
# - Security monitoring
# - Change tracking
# - Compliance reporting

examples.name: performance_metrics
examples.title: Performance Metrics Collection
examples.description: Query and collect performance metrics from vSphere objects using PerformanceManager. Retrieve CPU, memory, network, and disk metrics for VMs and hosts.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
anyhow = "1.0"
chrono = "0.4"

# Common metric counters:
# - cpu.usage.average
# - mem.usage.average
# - net.usage.average
# - disk.usage.average

examples.name: type_conversion
examples.title: Dynamic Type Casting and Conversion
examples.description: Use CastInto trait to safely convert between vSphere polymorphic types. Useful when dealing with device arrays or inheritance hierarchies.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"

# CastInto trait provides:
# - Safe downcasting
# - Type checking
# - Polymorphic object handling
# Common uses: devices, datastores, hosts

examples.name: root_objects_services
examples.title: Accessing vSphere Service Instances
examples.description: Access different vSphere service instances (VIM, EAM, PBM, VSLM, SMS) using RootObjects helper. Each service provides specialized management capabilities.
examples.dependencies:
[dependencies]
vim_rs = "0.2"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = ["macros"] }
log = "0.4"

# Service endpoints:
# - VIM: Core vCenter management
# - EAM: ESXi agent deployment
# - PBM: Storage policy management
# - VSLM: First-class disk management
# - SMS: Storage provider integration
